triggers: a kernel on NVIDIA B200 (GB200 / SM100) risks the '2. NaN landmine: `exp2(-inf - -inf)` in online softmax over maskable tiles' trap

payload.goal: Avoid a known trap on NVIDIA B200 (GB200 / SM100): 2. NaN landmine: `exp2(-inf - -inf)` in online softmax over maskable tiles

problem.statement: sm_100 Triton sparse-decode / split-K pitfalls -- 2. NaN landmine: `exp2(-inf - -inf)` in online softmax over maskable tiles

payload.attempted: A local online-softmax over a *subset* of keys (one split, one tile) works in testing. Full-kernel softmax over the whole TopK never tripped it.
payload.lesson: Any online softmax over a possibly-empty subset must guard the max before exponentiating: `m_safe = tl.where(m_new == -inf, 0.0, m_new)` and `alpha = tl.where(m_prev == -inf, 0.0, exp2(m_prev - m_safe))`. Splitting a working full-reduction into partial reductions *introduces* this hazard — add the guard at the same time.

established_fact.mechanism: Full-TopK softmax never hit it because "all 2048 entries padded" is implausible — but per-split, an empty split is common on sparse/short inputs.

payload.observed: When a split is **fully masked** (all-padding), `m_new = -inf`, and `exp2(m_prev - m_new) = exp2(-inf - -inf) = exp2(NaN) = NaN` silently poisons the accumulator. Surfaces only on shapes where an entire split can be empty.
payload.root_cause: Full-TopK softmax never hit it because "all 2048 entries padded" is implausible — but per-split, an empty split is common on sparse/short inputs.
